set.approach: The wall is reached from Crescent Meadow near Moro Rock by a long backcountry hike to Hamilton Lake, the nearest camp. A backcountry permit is required and overnight stays at the lake are limited. The south face of Angel Wings rises directly above the lake basin. The route climbs the south face by a crack system of wide grooves, beside the Rowell-Jones line and just left of it.

review.notes: Area page for trailhead and camp; AAJ note for the pillar and its position relative to Rowell-Jones.

set.approach: The wall is reached from Crescent Meadow near Moro Rock by a long backcountry hike to Hamilton Lake, the nearest camp. A backcountry permit is required and overnight stays at the lake are limited. The south face of Angel Wings rises directly above the lake basin. The route starts in the centre of the main south face, on the left-hand one of two crossing ramps whose X shape is visible a few hundred feet up.

review.notes: Area page for trailhead and camp; route page for the start on the south face.

set.approach: Follow the Bubbs Creek trail east from Road's End at Cedar Grove, the same long hike used for Charlotte Dome, to the camping area just beyond the Charlotte Creek crossing. Continue a short way along the trail until the big wall comes into view on the left. The route begins at a large pine a little uphill and to the right of the enormous white dihedral that opens the crystal band.
set.descent_text: From the top, descend west toward Charlotte Creek, the drainage that runs down toward Charlotte Dome, and follow it back to the Bubbs Creek trail.

review.notes: Route page: start at the pine, descent via Charlotte Creek to the west. Area page: trail approach from Road's End and the wall seen on the left past Charlotte Creek.

set.approach: Drive the Mineral King road to the Paradise Ridge trailhead, close to Atwell Mill campground. Hike the Paradise Ridge trail up to the ridge, then leave it and contour north-northwest cross-country, threading a few minor drainages, until the Fortress, and the gully under it, appear ahead; the whole way in is roughly six miles. Stay on the right (east) side of the gully until below the wall, cross it, and climb to the base. The line follows a corner and offwidth system on the east face.

review.notes: Area page: trailhead, ridge and cross-country line. AAJ report: about six miles from the trailhead, east-face corner system.
